key_insight: A transformer can adapt reward modeling to new human preference domains in context, but it needs an extra cue—human response time—to overcome bias and generalize robustly.
engineering_relevance: This enables more scalable RLHF systems that handle heterogeneous, previously unseen preference distributions without retraining separate reward models.
method: Use a transformer-based in-context reward learner fed with a small set of preference demonstrations.
Condition the model on human response time as an auxiliary signal to infer latent reward structure.
Test adaptation to unseen preference domains rather than only fixed known domains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a characterizable asymptotic bias for a standard transformer, and shows that adding response time allows successful adaptation to previously unseen preference domains.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the availability and quality of response-time signals, which can be noisy or hard to capture consistently in deployment.
paper_title: In-Context Reward Adaptation for Robust Preference Modeling
